subject: Communication
title: Steel-Manning: Arguing Against the Best Version
description: A 60-second lesson on Steel-Manning: Arguing Against the Best Version.

hook.text: A straw man attacks the weakest version of an argument. A steel man attacks the strongest.

buildup.text: Steel-manning means restating your opponent's argument in its best, most charitable form before arguing against it.

discovery.text: Daniel Dennett's rules: restate their position so clearly they say 'I wish I'd put it that way.' Then list agreements.

twist.text: Steel-manning is rare because it's hard. It requires genuinely understanding the other side — which sometimes changes your mind.

climax.text: If you can't steel-man the opposing view, you probably don't understand it well enough to argue against it effectively.

punchline.text: Beat the best version of the argument. Everything else is shadowboxing.

quiz.question: What does steel-manning an argument mean?
options: Restating it in its strongest form before arguing against it

details.summary: Steel manning is the practice of representing an opponent's argument in its strongest possible form before critiquing it. Instead of attacking a weak version, you strengthen it and then engage the strongest case. This produces more honest debate and more durable conclusions.
details.whyItMatters: Steel manning is the antidote to straw man arguments. It builds intellectual credibility and ensures your own position has survived the toughest possible challenges.
takeaways: Present the opposing view more strongly than they did
Defeating a strong argument is more meaningful than defeating a weak one
Steel manning earns respect and credibility from all sides

faq.question: How do you steel man an argument you strongly disagree with?
faq.answer: Find the most reasonable interpretation of what the person is saying. Ask yourself what a thoughtful, intelligent person could mean by this position. Look for the grain of truth even in views you reject. Present that strongest version before explaining why you still disagree.

faq.question: Is steel manning always appropriate?
faq.answer: It is most valuable in good-faith intellectual discussions. In situations involving bad-faith actors or positions that cause direct harm, extensive steel manning can give undue legitimacy. The key is distinguishing between ideas worth engaging with charitably and those that are simply dangerous.
